extracted.intended_audience: persons enlisted as earthquake observers/assistants for the Swiss Natural History Society (volunteer and professional field observers)
extracted.subtask_description: A scheduled checklist and organizational guidance for systematically observing and reporting earthquakes (for local observers and stations assigned by the Swiss commission). It specifies what to record about time, place, motion, effects, noises, minor phenomena, and local corroborating information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic investigation organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that a large number of observations at as many places as possible is necessary for the sufficient investigation of every earthquake; the commission enlists persons interested in investigations, assigns a tract/field to each member, provides instruments and a schedule of questions, and preserves collected accounts in an archive of earthquakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each commission member is expected to communicate with competent local assistants, place selected stations with instruments for special observations, furnish observers with the schedule of questions (to be answered as fully as possible), and request graphical representation of shock phases where possible; collected accounts are to be arranged and preserved in an earthquake archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: On what day was the earthquake noticed?
rubrics_metrics.description: On what day was the earthquake noticed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers should state the calendar day of observation; answer as fully as possible as part of the 17-question schedule supplied by the commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: At what hour?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the time of occurrence as precisely as possible; see also question on telegraph clock agreement for more precise timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clock agreement with telegraph clock
rubrics_metrics.description: How did your clock agree on the day, or, better, on the hour, of the earthquake, with the nearest telegraph clock?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comparison with a telegraph standard clock to improve precision of timing; note any known clock offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact place and observer situation
rubrics_metrics.description: Endeavor to furnish an exact description of the place of observation, the canton, town, situation, whether in the open or among buildings, in what story of the house; state in what position and what occupation the observer was when the shock was perceived?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give detailed location and immediate circumstances of the observer (indoors/outdoors, floor, activity) to contextualize perceived motion and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local ground/soil conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: On what kind of soil does the place of observation stand? Whether the surface be of rock, soil, or peat; depth of the ground to bed-rock, etc.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe substrate and depth to bedrock when known; such information aids interpretation of local amplification or duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and timing of shocks
rubrics_metrics.description: How many shocks were felt, and during what interval of time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record count and temporal spacing of felt shocks; note intervals between them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction and character of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: In what direction was the motion? Did it come from below, was it short and in a direction from side to side, or broad, surging in the form of waves, or only a trembling? In case there were more than one shock, was there a difference in the character of the different shocks? With what could the motion be compared, and how did it affect the observer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe perceived direction, nature (surging, trembling, lateral), differences between shocks, and analogies (e.g., like a wagon, like waves). Note physical effects on observer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction of trembling felt
rubrics_metrics.description: In what direction was the trembling of the earth felt?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify compass or relative direction of ground motion as perceived by the observer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of shocks and trembling
rubrics_metrics.description: How long did the shocks and the subsequent trembling seem to last?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimated durations for main shocks and lingering tremor; note subjective impressions of length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects produced by the shaking
rubrics_metrics.description: What effects did the shaking produce?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report damage, objects displaced, jars, falls, cracking, changes in water, or other physical consequences observed locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing from previous earthquakes
rubrics_metrics.description: How might this earthquake be distinguished from others which have previously been noticed by the same observers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare character, intensity, duration, direction, and effects with prior local events to help classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noise heard and character
rubrics_metrics.description: Was any noise heard, and, if so, what kind of a noise was it — like thunder, a clinking, a rattling, a clap, or a continuous noise, etc.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any audible phenomena, their quality, and loudness; note simultaneity with motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of noise relative to shaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the noise precede the shaking or follow it, and how long did it last in comparison with the duration of the shocks and of the intervals between them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether sounds came before, during, or after shaking and relative durations to aid source interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor phenomena observed
rubrics_metrics.description: What particular minor phenomena were observed? Were there, for instance, anything peculiar in the behavior of animals; any drying up, or troubling, or breaking out again of springs; any peculiar rustling in the woods, any gusts of wind simultaneous with the shocks, or abnormal features of the weather?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note all ancillary phenomena (animal behavior, spring/well changes, flora/agitation, winds, weather anomalies) that accompanied the shocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations regarding lakes
rubrics_metrics.description: What was noticed with regard to the lakes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report changes in lakes: seiches, waves, turbidity, level changes, or other observable lake phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lighter shocks relative to main shock
rubrics_metrics.description: Were lighter shocks felt before or after the main shocks, and at what time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record aftershocks or foreshocks with approximate timing relative to the principal shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional neighborhood observations and contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you mention any other observations made by your acquaintances or in your neighborhood, or can you give the addresses of persons who are able to answer all of these questions, or a part of them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide corroborating reports from neighbors and contact information for other observers who can supply fuller answers; help the commission extend its data coverage.
